conviction.explanation: 36% revenue growth, margin expansion and increasing Q2 FCF support profitable foundry participation with internally funded capex and large liquid surplus.22x forecast earnings has operating support, but inventory, overseas returns, Taiwan exposure and RSI near 88 constrain conviction.

executive_summary:
TSMC supports a positive foundry-growth thesis independent of investment gains. Revenue grew 36%, operating margin reached 60.3%, and Q2 FCF increased to NT$287.36bn from NT$199.85bn. H1 CFO exceeded capex by NT$635.576bn, with liquid assets exceeding interest-bearing debt by NT$2,486.33bn.

Inventory days rose to 87 and prospective operating-margin guidance of 56–58% is below the peak. Taiwan exposure and overseas execution remain economically material regardless of liquidity. At 22x estimated forward earnings, continued profitable demand can compensate those risks, but 35.31x trailing earnings and RSI near 88 argue against treating current entry as effortless or peak margins as permanent.
bull_case: Sustained profitable foundry demand and cash-funded capacity could support growth even with margins below the Q2 peak.
bear_case: Inventory normalization, weaker fab returns or geopolitical loss could impair earnings and shareholder value despite financial resilience.
key_uncertainties: Incremental overseas-capacity returns and inventory conversion.
Guidance is prospective; investment gains are excluded from recurring growth.
catalysts_upcoming: Actual delivery against Q3 revenue$44.6–45.8bn guidance with profitable cash conversion would support continued demand.
Comparable cash exceeding capex with moderating inventory days would strengthen internally funded growth.

correlation_notes: Sector: Technology — use sector-specific catalysts and risks in the thesis.
risk_assessment.max_drawdown_scenario: Historical max drawdown: 56.5% over available price history. Projected worst case (2-sigma): ~66.1% from current $482.30.

action_plan.stop_rationale: 2x ATR-14 ($10.12) below entry — invalidates the setup
action_plan.target_rationale: TP1 = nearest technical resistance (SMA-200, BB-upper, or 52w high). TP2 = 52w high / +15% stretch. Consider scaling out: sell half at TP1, let the rest ride to TP2.

research_verdict.thesis: TSMC supports a profitable foundry-growth purchase through 36% revenue growth, 60.3% operating margin and internally funded investment. The bull adds actual Q2 FCF growth to NT$287.36bn, independently supporting owner-cash participation beyond investment gains. Estimated 22x forward earnings has substantive operating support, while margin normalization, inventory and Taiwan exposure keep conviction bounded rather than serving as automatic vetoes.
research_verdict.strongest_counterexample: Inventory days rose to 87, guided operating margin falls to 56-58%, and Taiwan concentration cannot be diversified away by NT$2,486.33bn liquid surplus; overseas fab returns may disappoint even with financially funded expansion.
invalidation_conditions: Reported operating margin below the prior comparable 49.6% with year-on-year revenue decline would invalidate the operating-improvement basis.
Comparable H1 CFO no longer exceeding capex, from NT$635.576bn positive cash after capex, would undermine the internally funded capacity thesis.
decisive_factors: Q2 FCF increased from NT$199.85bn; cash funding is observed and not reliant on Vanguard gains.
Prospective margin normalization need not return profitability to the prior-year level, but guidance is not achieved performance.
